Tidy and Glance Methods for the Fraction of Missing Information

Source: R/fraction_missing_information.R
tidy.dmar_fmi.Rd

tidy() returns one row per parameter of a fraction_missing_information table, with the FMI as the estimate, its percentile limits, and the effective sample size; glance() returns a one-row summary of the table.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'dmar_fmi'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'dmar_fmi'
glance(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A dmar_fmi object returned by fraction_missing_information.

...

Unused.

Value

tidy() returns a data.frame with columns term (the parameter), group, estimate (its FMI), estimand ("fmi", which names the estimate, so that results_sentence on a row reports "fmi = 0.24, 90% CI [0.18, 0.32]" and not the FMI as the parameter's value), ci_lower, ci_upper, conf_level (all three NA without the percentile interval), and N_effective. glance() returns a one-row data.frame with n_parameters, fmi_max, fmi_median, N (the cases the fit used, summed over groups), and information.

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

fit <- fa_confirmatory(data = holzinger_swineford,
             factors = list(spatial = c("t1_visual_perception",
               "t2_cubes", "t3_paper_form_board", "t4_lozenges",
               "t25_paper_form_board_r", "t26_flags")),
             missing = "fiml", output = "fit")
fmi <- fraction_missing_information(fit)
generics::tidy(fmi)
